messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a big spike in cache misses and tail latency after the kernel-selector change rolled yesterday. p95 for seqlen=512 jumped from ~18ms to ~42ms. Anyone else seeing this?
ben: Yup, got the same alert. Dumping quick profile: 
```
period: 03:12-03:45
requests: 72k
cache_hit_rate: 78% -> 62%
p50/p95: 12ms / 18ms -> 20ms / 42ms
most affected: model=redwood-13b, arch=A100, seqlen_bin=512
```
chao: My quick glance — kernel-selector started attaching an extra "arch_tag" to the KV key last deploy (for arch-aware kernel routing). Seems the key format changed so old entries aren't matched. :frowning:
maria: ugh. Did we do a migration plan? I thought kernel selector change was supposed to be compatible.
ben: It was marked compatible but the key version bump was implicit. Old driver writes keys as `model:v1:<seqbin>:<kv>` new writes `model:v1:arch=<arch>:<seqbin>:<kv>`. So reads won't find the old ones.
elain: (typo: i'm elaine) We need to avoid mass invalidation. Options: backfill old keys, double-write for X hours, or implement a layered lookup that tries both key shapes. Double-write seems simplest short-term.
sam: Double-write + lookup-fallback is reasonable. For persistence, how long do we keep old format? suggest 48h for safe rollouts. Also we should include seqbin in key explicitly (we already are) because selector heuristics re-bucketed some sequences.
chao: Another thing — kernel autotuner changed seqlen bin boundaries which means "seqbin" semantics shifted. That explains why some 256->512 transitions are cold. Need a stable seqbin mapping version in keys.
maria: So concrete plan: 1) revert implicit key version change or 2) implement compatibility layer that tries previous key shapes + records salt/version in metadata store for 72h. Which do we prefer?
ben: Revert is safer but slower (needs rollback). Compatibility layer can be hot-fixed in the driver quickly. I'll open a tiny PR with fallback read logic that checks old key patterns (tries up to 3 variants) and double-writes new keys for writes.
elaine: For persistence TTL, we should avoid indefinite back-compat. Propose: keep fallback checks for 7 days max, but double-write for 48h only. We'll also emit metrics when fallback path used so we can clean up.
sam: Also want to avoid extra lookup cost on hot path. Implementation: on read, check primary key; on miss, spawn an async check of fallback keys and if found, migrate entry back to primary in background. That avoids synchronously increasing latency.
chao: Good. For salt rotation on driver upgrades — instead of baking salt into key directly, put a small key-version byte in the key and store salt lookup table in etcd/metadata. That way, driver restarts with new salt still consult older key-versions for a window.
maria: Can we add a quick perf check so fallback doesn't regress p99? Maybe feature-flag the async fallback and gate by a small sample.
ben: I'll attach a profiler before/after. Early sim shows async fallback keeps p95 within 5% but reduces miss storm over time.
ci-bot: deploybot: v2.4.9-kernel-selector rolled to canary (5 nodes) — health ok, no crashes.
elaine: Action items: ben to PR compatibility layer + metrics; chao to add key-version and metadata schema; sam to add async migration helper; maria to run canary perf tests and report p95/p99. Owner: ben for immediate fix.
maria: Thanks all — let's aim to have the fallback live in canary today and monitor cache_hit_rate and p95 for seqlen=512. :thumbsup:
